solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Very odd area around gym (6)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so the word for area is wrapped round the word for gym

blocks.note: physical education, the school gym lesson

annotation.surface: Someone finds a district built round a gymnasium very strange.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Area' for a ward is loose, but a ward is a defined division of a town or hospital, which is fair enough.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a warped mind or sense of humour is twisted, so very odd.

entries.clue: Wife is … um … older partner? (5)

annotation.surface: A husband hesitates before admitting his wife is the older one.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the hesitant husband concedes that his wife is the wiser, more seasoned partner, 'older' suggesting the experience that brings wisdom.
annotation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue is a husband's grudging admission, and age is traditionally what makes one wiser.

entries.clue: Move? What, and move around? (7)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means surrounding, so the word for move goes round the word for what

blocks.note: to stir or move someone to action; 'and' only joins

annotation.surface: A puzzled listener asks whether they are being told to move house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Move' appears twice: first as the definition, move to new housing, then in the wordplay in its rousing sense. The question mark flags that rehousing is only one kind of move.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: rehousing people is one way of moving them.

entries.clue: What lovers may reveal so no time is wasted (8)

indicatorNotes.wasted: 'wasted' means ruined, so the letters of so no time are wrecked and rebuilt

annotation.surface: Lovers show their hand quickly so no time is lost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'So no time is wasted' reads as a phrase of haste; 'wasted' is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: what lovers open up about is how they feel.

entries.clue: Rugby players tackling over a large pitch (8)

indicatorNotes.tackling: 'tackling' means grabbing hold of, so the rugby players hold the letter for over

blocks.note: props are front-row forwards in rugby

annotation.surface: Rugby forwards make tackles on a big field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' pulls toward the rugby field; it is a sales pitch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sales pitch is a proposal put to a buyer.

entries.clue: Those needed if we go to see ABBA? (6,7)

annotation.definition: Those needed if we go to see ABBA?

blocks.note: the surface suggests concert tickets for fans

blocks.clueFragment: if we go to see ABBA?
blocks.note: read as a route: go from A to B, then B back to A, as the palindrome ABBA spells out

annotation.surface: Fans need tickets for an ABBA concert.
annotation.walkthrough: The band's name is a journey there and back, A to B and B to A, which is what a return ticket covers. The comeback tour adds a second nod.
annotation.definitionFit: A return ticket pays for the outward and homeward legs, the A-B-B-A trip.

entries.clue: Head of Penguin right to get rid of author (6)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its front, so only its first letter is taken

blocks.note: to oust is to get rid of

annotation.surface: Penguin's publishing chief wants the right to drop a writer.
annotation.walkthrough: Penguin is the publisher, so the surface is a boardroom dispute over a writer, and the answer is a writer too.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Marcel Proust, the French novelist of In Search of Lost Time.

entries.clue: Usual clothes FBI agents cut up (7)

indicatorNotes.clothes: 'clothes' as a verb means dresses, so the word for usual is wrapped round the agents

blocks.note: a set routine is the usual one

annotation.surface: FBI agents in their normal clothes are upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun; it is the verb. 'Cut up' also suggests upset, but here it means divided.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to segment something is to divide it into parts.

entries.clue: Obstruction in new toilet makes one wee on foot (6,3)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the obstruction inside the rearranged toilet
indicatorNotes.new: 'new' means made afresh, so toilet's letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: an obstruction or hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

annotation.surface: A blocked new toilet leads someone to wee on their foot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wee' is Scottish for small, not an act at the toilet: the answer is one small thing on a foot.
annotation.definitionFit: Reading 'wee' as small, the smallest of the five toes on each foot is the one meant.

entries.clue: Belief in mental faculty? (6,2,7)

blocks.note: a shared doctrine or outlook, which is what the answer is
the surface means a power of the mind; but a university faculty is a department of learning, so this is an academic department devoted to thinking

annotation.surface: Someone believes in the powers of the mind.
annotation.walkthrough: A university faculty is also called a school, so a 'mental faculty' can be read as a school devoted to thought.
annotation.definitionFit: A school of thought is a body of shared belief, and the clue dresses it as a university department.

entries.clue: On a roll? Skip surplus (13)

blocks.note: a bun is a bread roll
to skip is to dance lightly

annotation.surface: Someone on a winning streak decides to skip the extra.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On a roll' reads as a lucky streak, but it splits into on and a bread roll.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a surplus is more than is needed, an excess.

entries.clue: Ordinary rake, metal parts (7)

indicatorNotes.parts: 'parts' as a verb means separates, so the rake is split open to hold the metal

blocks.note: a roué is a dissolute man, a rake

annotation.surface: An everyday garden rake with metal parts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool; it is a libertine. 'Parts' looks like a noun; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: routine work is ordinary, everyday work.

entries.clue: Rumours of sightings all started right here (7)

annotation.definition: Rumours of sightings all started right here

indicatorNotes.all started: the words all give only the letter they start with

blocks.note: well in the sense of all right, fine

annotation.surface: UFO rumours began in this very place.
annotation.walkthrough: Roswell, New Mexico, is where the 1947 flying-saucer rumours began, so the whole clue describes the town.
annotation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue describes the town where the famous 1947 UFO-crash story began.

entries.clue: Those somewhat into recycling energy? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.into: 'into' means going inside, so the word for somewhat sits within the rearranged energy
indicatorNotes.recycling: recycling turns material into something new, so energy's letters are reprocessed

annotation.surface: People who are fairly keen on renewable energy.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a Green Party is into recycling and clean energy.
annotation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue describes an environmentalist party's supporters, keen on recycling and renewable energy.

entries.clue: Rally is concluding (9)

blocks.note: inferring, as in 'I gather you are busy'

annotation.surface: A political rally is coming to its end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concluding' pushes toward finishing; it means inferring.
annotation.definitionFit: A rally is a mass gathering, and to gather is to conclude from what you hear.

entries.clue: Now, say? Almost (4)

indicatorNotes.Almost: 'almost' means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: STATE, to say, without its last letter E

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether now is nearly the moment.
annotation.walkthrough: STAT is medical shorthand, from Latin statim, for immediately.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical term: a doctor ordering a test stat wants it immediately.

entries.clue: Meet up with us, I propose (8)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' means read upwards, so us is turned round

blocks.note: to table a motion is to propose it

annotation.surface: Someone suggests getting together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is an old adjective meaning fitting, as in 'it is meet and right', not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic sense: meet as an adjective means fitting or proper.

entries.clue: Drunk’s knocked back hard stuff (4)

indicatorNotes.knocked back: 'knocked back' means sent backwards, so the drunk is turned round

annotation.surface: A drunk has downed some strong spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' reads as spirits, but 'stuff' alone is the definition, as in 'stuff and nonsense'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its nonsense sense: 'stuff!' and 'tosh!' both dismiss rubbish.

entries.clue: Native American writer born in France (7)

blocks.note: née, French for born, used before maiden names

annotation.surface: A Native American author was born in France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In France' flags the French word for born rather than a birthplace.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Shawnee are a Native American people of the Ohio valley.

entries.clue: Lecturer’s wife meeting pawnbroker (5,5)

blocks.note: Cockney: 'my old Dutch' is my wife

annotation.surface: An academic's wife goes to see a pawnbroker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecturer' is not an academic here but someone who lectures you sternly; 'my old Dutch' is Cockney for a wife.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to talk like a Dutch uncle is to lecture someone bluntly.

entries.clue: For crying out loud, see Dorothy? (7)

blocks.note: Dorothy Lamour, the film star of the Road movies

annotation.surface: An exasperated 'for crying out loud' followed by a trip to see someone called Dorothy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For crying out loud' reads as an exclamation; split off 'For' and the rest is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a clamour is a loud outcry from many voices.

entries.clue: Container of firm pastry cases (6)

indicatorNotes.cases: 'cases' as a verb means encloses, so the pastry wraps round the firm

blocks.note: a flan is a pastry tart

annotation.surface: A box of a company's pastry cases.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pastry cases' looks like a noun phrase; 'cases' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loanword: a flacon is a small stoppered bottle, especially for perfume.

entries.clue: Contacted me about having been ill (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means turned round, as in about-face, so me is turned round

annotation.surface: Someone got in touch to say they had been unwell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning'; it is the turning instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sending an email is one way of contacting someone.

entries.clue: More sides to cut for quarry (7)

indicatorNotes.sides to: the sides of a word are its two ends, its outer letters

annotation.surface: A quarry needs more of its faces cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' looks like the pit or the hunted animal; it is the verb, to dig out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stone is quarried by digging it out of the ground.

entries.clue: Attorney is into sport for now (5)

indicatorNotes.is into: 'is into' read literally means goes inside, so the attorney enters the word for sport

blocks.note: to toy is to sport or play

annotation.surface: A lawyer is currently keen on sport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is into' looks like 'is keen on', and 'sport' looks like a game; it is the verb, to play.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'today' means at the present time, nowadays.

entries.clue: Some travellers in cab sent on trips in advance (9,6)

indicatorNotes.trips: 'trips' means stumbles, so cab sent on falls into a new order
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the rearranged letters inside the word for advance

blocks.note: an inroad is an advance into territory

annotation.surface: Tourists send a taxi ahead of their trips.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trips' looks like journeys, fitting the travellers, but it is the anagram signal. The Innocents Abroad is Mark Twain's book about naive American tourists.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: naive tourists, after Twain's travel book The Innocents Abroad.

entries.clue: Woolly farm animal (8)

blocks.note: a noun here: British for a knitted jumper, and a thick fisherman's sweater fits
a breed of dairy cow named after one of the Channel Islands

annotation.surface: A sheep with a thick fleece.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints a sheep, but 'woolly' is a noun: British for a knitted jumper.
annotation.definitionFit: A woolly is a sweater and a guernsey is one; a Guernsey is also a dairy cow breed.

entries.clue: Close attention given to British in New York (6)

indicatorNotes.given to: 'given to' means handed on to, so British is attached after attention
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places that pair inside New York

blocks.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

annotation.surface: A British visitor to New York gets close attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close attention' reads as one phrase; 'Close' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nearby shop is close at hand.
